critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The target identity and approach stage were settled, but the instruction did not specify how to recover the container's grasp-axis world centre from its projected silhouette, accounting for the visible faces' heights rather than back-projecting the silhouette centre at an assumed height. For the container near [107,81], that geometric refinement should give approximately x=-0.0876, y=-0.0791 and square-side yaw=0.3398, then an open-hand approach at z=0.20. My estimated x=-0.098 was just over 1 cm off; no additional historical fact was needed.

The wrist-view alignment rule needed to specify projecting the selected container's top-face centre onto its physical top-height plane, rather than using its silhouette centre or the table plane. Here the selected top face is near wrist pixel [141,146]; with the given calibration its centre is approximately world [-0.0696,-0.1423]. Descend to that x,y at z=0.0633 and close, with yaw approximately 0.1437. My estimated x=-0.100 was a geometric localization error, not an identity or completion-memory error.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Two geometric-localization failures occurred despite correct target identity and task stage. After returning the first requested container and withdrawing, the policy correctly selected the second requested container but placed its open-hand approach just over 1 cm away in x. In another case, the hand was above the first requested container and correctly chose a closing descent, but its estimated grasp position was about 3 cm off in x. The carried target_locations and completed_lifts were correct in both situations. These are SUFFICIENCY failures in the action instruction's localization procedure, not missing historical information or memory-transition failures.

Replace the generic direction to estimate the container centre from visible geometry with an explicit distinction between identity localization and grasp localization. target_locations contains whole-silhouette image centres only to identify containers; those pixels are not projections of the grasp axis at a known height. Once the selected container is identified, locate its physical top-face corners and recover the top-face centre, preferably using the current calibrated wrist view together with the front view. Back-project those corners onto the physical top-face plane, not the table plane, and obtain the world x,y centre from the reconstructed square. Do not use the centre of the entire silhouette, which includes side faces at different heights. Determine the top-plane height from the container geometry and calibrated simultaneous views; where needed, fit a horizontal square top and its vertical side faces jointly to the observations rather than choosing an arbitrary plane height.

For explicit back-projection, with world-to-camera calibration R,t, the camera centre is C=-R^T t and the world ray through pixel [u,v] is d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]. For a top plane at world height h, its intersection is C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Reconstruct the top corners this way, average their world coordinates for the grasp-axis centre, and determine yaw from the reconstructed square edges rather than raw image-edge angles. Use the front view to establish identity and corroborate geometry, and the wrist view to refine the selected target, not to switch to a different nearby container.

Apply that recovered x,y both to the open approach at z=0.20 m and to the closing descent at z=0.0633 m. A hand already near approach height should descend to the independently reconstructed target centre even if its reported TCP x,y is displaced by motion error. Neither the current TCP position nor an assumed-height back-projection of the silhouette centre should substitute for this reconstruction. Keep the existing target-order, lift-counting, return, withdrawal, and gripper rules unchanged; no new memory field is required.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Estimate each selected container's world centre and square-edge orientation from calibrated front and wrist views. Use camera projection and the visible container geometry rather than interpreting image pixels as world coordinates.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Distinguish container identity from grasp geometry. target_locations stores whole-silhouette image centres for identifying containers, not projections of their grasp axes at a known height. After identifying the selected container in the front view, locate its physical top-face corners using the calibrated current front and wrist views. Use the wrist view to refine that same container, not to switch to a nearby one. Recover the horizontal top-plane height from the container geometry and simultaneous calibrated views; where necessary, jointly fit a horizontal square top and vertical side faces to the observations. Do not choose an arbitrary plane height or project the silhouette centre onto the table. For world-to-camera calibration R,t, the camera centre is C=-R^T t and the world ray through pixel [u,v] is d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]. Its intersection with a top plane of height h is C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Reconstruct the physical top corners on this plane and average their world coordinates to obtain the grasp-axis x,y centre. Determine yaw from reconstructed square edges, not raw image-edge angles. Use this recovered x,y for both the open approach at z=0.20 m and the closing descent at z=0.0633 m, refining it with current imagery before descent.

fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: During the video cycle, identify which container descends over each requested cube colour. Follow those containers continuously across the shuffle frames, including exchanges between identical-looking containers. Write their final front-image silhouette centres as [u,v] pixel pairs in requested colour order. Do not infer identity from the final arrangement alone or assume a container returned to its original identity because the arrangement repeats. Carry this list unchanged at every act cycle. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [u,v] front-image container-centre locations, in pixels, at the end of the demonstration, one for each requested cube colour in instruction order. Identify the container that originally covered each requested cube and follow its continuous motion through every shuffle; record its final location, not the cube's original location. Include no distractors. Use the centre of the entire visible container silhouette consistently. Set this list at the video cycle and retain it throughout execution, including after a selected container moves. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]

fields.name: completed_lifts
fields.description: Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment once when this cycle's motion frames show the next requested container rising with the closed gripper from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height. The container must move with the hand; a newly exposed cube supports confirmation. Count the observed lift, not a lift you are about to command. Do not increment for a static elevated grasp, a downward return, an open-hand withdrawal, or a grasp closure at low height. If the motion executes no steps, retain the count. Otherwise retain the incoming value unless this successful new lift is observed. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers already lifted successfully in instruction order. Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment at the first act cycle showing the selected container carried upward from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height with the gripper closed. Do not increment for closing at grasp height, returning a container, withdrawing with an open gripper, or continuing to hold an already-counted container. Retain the count otherwise. e.g. 1

texts.action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution starts with an open hand above the scene and completed_lifts equal to zero. Use target_locations to identify the requested containers in the current front image; the list records identities by their final demonstration locations, not their initial cube locations. Distinguish container identity from grasp geometry. target_locations stores whole-silhouette image centres for identifying containers, not projections of their grasp axes at a known height. After identifying the selected container in the front view, locate its physical top-face corners using the calibrated current front and wrist views. Use the wrist view to refine that same container, not to switch to a nearby one. Recover the horizontal top-plane height from the container geometry and simultaneous calibrated views; where necessary, jointly fit a horizontal square top and vertical side faces to the observations. Do not choose an arbitrary plane height or project the silhouette centre onto the table. For world-to-camera calibration R,t, the camera centre is C=-R^T t and the world ray through pixel [u,v] is d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]. Its intersection with a top plane of height h is C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Reconstruct the physical top corners on this plane and average their world coordinates to obtain the grasp-axis x,y centre. Determine yaw from reconstructed square edges, not raw image-edge angles. Use this recovered x,y for both the open approach at z=0.20 m and the closing descent at z=0.0633 m, refining it with current imagery before descent. Robot-left is +y, which appears on the right of the front image. Grasp the container, not the cube.

Apply the following rules to the observed state, accounting for a lift observed in this cycle before selecting the action. With an empty open hand and an unfinished target, select target_locations[completed_lifts]. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20 m, move to its world centre at z=0.20 m with the gripper open. Point straight down, roll=3.1416 and pitch=0, and align yaw with the container's opposing square sides. Infer the container centre independently of the reported TCP: long motions can stop roughly a centimetre short.

With the open hand above the selected container at approximately z=0.20 m, descend to the independently reconstructed grasp-axis centre at z=0.0633 m and close the gripper. Refine that centre from the current calibrated wrist and front imagery using the top-face reconstruction above. A small approach-motion error does not require another approach waypoint: correct x,y during descent. Neither the reported TCP x,y nor an assumed-height projection of the whole-silhouette centre substitutes for the reconstructed target centre. With the closed fingers around the container at this low height, raise its centre vertically to z=0.20 m, maintaining yaw and keeping the gripper closed. Fingers separated approximately 0.018 m each and a container between them indicate a grasp; do not release at this stage.

When a successful lift has just been observed and another requested target remains, return the held container before approaching the next one: keep the current TCP x,y and orientation, lower to z=0.070 m, and open at arrival. When the hand is open at this low return height, withdraw vertically at the current x,y to approximately z=0.147 m, remaining open. With the open hand at this withdrawal height, approach the next target at z=0.20 m. Do not regrasp the returned container merely because it is beneath the hand. completed_lifts distinguishes that completed target from the next requested one.

When the last requested container is grasped, lift it to z=0.20 m with the gripper closed; no return or extra container is required. If another cycle occurs after all requested lifts are confirmed, keep holding and wait briefly for termination.

For an unmatched or uncertain state, preserve the stored identities and completion count. Use the current wrist and front views to recover alignment. If empty and too low for safe lateral travel, withdraw vertically with the gripper open before approaching the unfinished target. If a grasp visibly failed, reopen while moving at least 5 mm, then realign and retry the same target without incrementing completed_lifts. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when only observation is needed.
